new_findings_today.title: Root-cause fix for the week's build-failure/statement-timeout saga shipped and verified live: find_nearby_destinations is now cached
new_findings_today.detail: Commit ecb3548b (2026-08-13T23:59:59 UTC) directly answers the question this QA process has been tracking since NEW-2026-08-03-002: measured this session (per the commit's own pg_stat_statements evidence), every individual query suspected of being 'slow' was actually healthy (dharmasthala getDestination 180ms, hill-station quiz query 276ms, find_nearby_destinations itself only 97ms in isolation) — the real problem was CONTENTION, specifically find_nearby_destinations running uncached on every destination-hub render and being called ~1,010 times per production build (3 workers prerendering 5,464 pages concurrently against the same DB), while being by far the single largest consumer of DB time site-wide. The fix moves it into the existing lib/cached-data.ts unstable_cache pattern used elsewhere in the codebase, with a throw-not-degrade failure mode consistent with the same reasoning already documented on fetchAllRows. NOT claimed as fully fixed: the commit itself is explicit that the anon role's 3-second statement_timeout (vs 8s for authenticated/authenticator) is the tighter structural constraint on exactly the public, SEO-critical pages that matter most, and that raising it was attempted this session and blocked by a permission classifier — this needs the founder to approve directly.
new_findings_today.evidence: Diff read directly: apps/web/src/app/[locale]/destination/[id]/page.tsx (-59/+... refactored to call the new cached accessor) and apps/web/src/lib/cached-data.ts (+103 lines, getCachedNearbyDestinations via unstable_cache, tag ref-nearby-destinations-v1) — confirmed via grep today. Vercel 24h runtime-error check: 6 error groups found, ALL on the OLD deployment (dpl_7eDCgFSnzrD53Kqe1doDCGbjb93s) between 2026-08-13T12:04–12:42 UTC (getDestination(dharmasthala) 57014, getMonthData(jabalpur,september) 57014, getMonthData(rishikesh,july) upstream timeout) — 0 error groups on the new deployment (dpl_3jXqQHy3UptK113app93MqXCGQ45, live since ~00:22 UTC, ~2h of traffic by the time of this check). Today's own destination-page TTFBs (Section B) were elevated on first-hit (up to 5,495ms) but this is the well-established cold-ISR-cache-after-deploy pattern, not a regression — every outlier re-probed to 128-170ms on second hit, actually faster than most prior weeks' warm times.
new_findings_today.recommendation: Keep watching — a ~2h clean window is encouraging but not conclusive; worth another explicit check next run for any 57014 recurrence on the new deployment specifically. Separately, still worth the founder's attention: (1) approve raising the anon role's statement_timeout from 3s to 8s (blocked on permission, not effort); (2) apply the same cached-data.ts treatment to /explore's own inline queries (NEW-2026-08-03-002), which this fix explicitly did not touch.

new_findings_today.title: A real, business-relevant bug — the newsletter signup success confirmation never rendered — was found and fixed by the team today, directly tied to the newsletter Northstar metric
new_findings_today.detail: Commit 1809adce (found by running the e2e suite against production, 22 failed/114 passed at the start of that session) identified that both email-capture surfaces (save-list-email-prompt.tsx and saved-list-capture.tsx) computed a `visible` flag with `if (status === "success") return false`, then unmounted the whole component when `!visible` — so the moment a subscribe call succeeded, the component vanished, and the fully-written, fully-translated (en+hi) success message ('Check your inbox to confirm') was dead code that could never render. Because the newsletter is double opt-in, a visitor who submits and sees the box silently disappear has no idea they need to check their inbox, so they never confirm, so they never become a subscriber. The commit message explicitly frames this against the site's own newsletter Northstar (>=10 confirmed emails/week, next read 2026-08-27, currently 0 signups / 5 subs all-time per that commit) — not claiming this explains the flat metric, but noting it has to be ruled out before blaming the offer itself.
new_findings_today.evidence: Read the commit's full diff directly rather than trusting the message: the `if (status === "success") return false` early-return is removed, and the prompt now stays mounted through the success state. NOT independently re-verified by triggering a live signup this session — deliberately avoided submitting the real email-capture form, since that would be entering personal data into a form and submitting it, which needs explicit user permission this unattended run cannot obtain. new_findings_today.title: Business Report generator leaks raw technical text (incl. commit hashes) into the persona that is explicitly supposed to have none — a real, previously-undiscovered qa/_lib/build_report.js bug, found by this run's own verification step
new_findings_today.detail: SKILL.md defines the Business Owner Report as 'No code, no commit hashes.' Reading the actually-generated NakshIQ_Business_Report.docx today (not just checking file size/XML validity) found two places where build_report.js violates that contract: (1) the shared header() function (called by ALL three personas, build_report.js lines 75-81) prints the full raw `run.executor` narrative verbatim — which routinely contains commit hashes, file paths, and SQL/implementation detail — at the top of the Business Report, not just the Developer/QA ones; (2) buildBusiness()'s 'Detail on today's findings' section (lines 223-230) loops over every f.new_findings_today entry and prints its raw `detail` field verbatim, regardless of whether business_summary.whats_changed already covers the same ground in plain language — so today's business docx contains phrases like 'Commit ecb3548b... pg_stat_statements evidence... lib/cached-data.ts unstable_cache pattern' directly under a heading meant to be code-free. This is very likely a LONGSTANDING bug (build_report.js's own header comment says it was reconstructed from scratch on 2026-06-05), not something introduced today — it's just unusually visible this week because today's run.executor and finding `detail` fields happen to cite short git hashes inline and explicit file/table names more prominently than most prior weeks' narratives did. Likely undiscovered until now because prior verification steps checked file size and XML well-formedness (both of which pass fine) but not persona-appropriateness of the actual rendered text.
new_findings_today.evidence: Extracted and read the Business Report's actual text content (unzip word/document.xml, strip tags) as part of this run's verification step, rather than only checking size/XML-validity. Found the literal strings 'ecb3548b', '1809adce', '71d248e7', '98d5e927', 'f1a055c0', '47d80bb1' (a Vercel MCP server id, not even a commit hash) all present in NakshIQ_Business_Report.docx. Root cause confirmed by reading qa/_lib/build_report.js directly: header() at lines 75-81 is shared by all three BUILDERS with no persona branch on the executor line, and buildBusiness() at lines 223-230 prints n.detail unconditionally.
new_findings_today.recommendation: Not fixed in this run — this is a change to shared report-generation code, out of scope for an unattended daily QA pass to make unsupervised. Suggested fix for a future session: in header(), only print the full r.executor line for developer/qa personas (business could get a one-line 'Automated daily check completed in N minutes' instead); in buildBusiness()'s 'Detail on today's findings' section, either drop it entirely (business_summary.whats_changed/bottom_line already exist specifically to cover this ground) or print only n.title + n.recommendation, never n.detail. Filed in the same family as the already-known, still-open NEW-2026-07-07-004 and NEW-2026-08-10-003 build_report.js field-drift issues — worth fixing all three together next time someone is in that file.
